Reference / template/compile

template/compile#

Text templates: {{name}} filled from strings.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let greeting = TextTemplate("Hello, {{user.name}}! You have {{user.unread}} new messages.");
greeting.string(["user.name": "Ada", "user.unread": "3"]);
greeting.write(data: TemplateBindings(texts), destination: Stdout());

Description#

Text templates: {{name}} filled from strings.

Names are dotted paths; {{! comment }} is dropped. Nothing is escaped (use template/html for HTML). The whole source is checked before any value is looked up; a missing value is MissingTemplateValue. Sections and partials are template/sections.

New code uses template/engine's Template (#178), the one engine over Json, with sections, partials and HTML escaping. This module holds the scanner that engine parses with; TextTemplate stays here, under the engine, as the flat loop over that scanner's literals and values for TemplateStrings data (TemplateBindings now keeps its values in one Json document).

Public API#

object TextTemplate#

object TextTemplate

Lazy plain template with explicit nominal string data. Example: TextTemplate("Hello {{name}}!").string(data) -> "Hello Ada!". source() returns original text. Each string(data) validates the entire program before querying data, then queries each occurrence once from left to right. Values are inserted literally, never recompiled, coerced or HTML escaped. Custom failures and MissingTemplateValue propagate unchanged; no partial text.

Grammar: {{ path }}, {{! comment }}, {{{{ and }}}} for literal delimiters. Only ASCII space/tab trims variable boundaries. Ordinary text stays exact. Whole-line comments remove their indentation and following LF/CRLF; inline comments remove only their tag. Paths split literal dots and retain case. Sections/partials/trusted markup are explicitly unsupported in this slice. See docs/std/template-guide.md for pending extensions and exact exclusions.

Optional limits: maximum_input scalars, maximum_nodes instructions, maximum_output UTF-8 bytes; defaults 1048576,10000,1048576. All nonnegative; negative configuration fails immediately. Empty text accepts all-zero limits. Invalid source/bounds throw TemplateFailure with original scalar coordinates. Output bounds stop before subsequent lookups; UTF-8 preflight is incremental. No I/O or implicit close of data. Okkama program objects are scope-owned; completed strings retain their own data and outlive template/source scope. Run: okkama run -t std/template/compile.ok

TextTemplate.write#

write(data is TemplateStrings, destination is WritingText) is void

Explicit borrowed output. Complete validation precedes effects. Each next contribution is byte-budgeted before its first chunk; successful prefixes remain visible on later failure. At most 1024 scalars/4096 UTF-8 bytes per write, no empty chunks, newline, flush or close. No full-result buffer.

object TemplateInstruction#

object TemplateInstruction

Internal immutable flat instructions; no native program state escapes or is retained. Grammar observation occurs through TemplateProgram.instructions(). Internal structured mode additionally retains tag (#,^,/,>) and original offset for TemplateTree. The default mode keeps TextTemplate's flat grammar.
